Leaf Blight.description: Large irregular brown necrotic patches spreading from the leaf margins, typical of bacterial or fungal blight under humid conditions.
Leaf Blight.treatment: Remove and destroy affected leaves, improve airflow between rows, and apply a copper-based fungicide every 7–10 days.

Powdery Mildew.description: Pale, low-saturation powdery film across the leaf surface caused by fungal mycelium growth in warm, dry days with humid nights.
Powdery Mildew.treatment: Spray a potassium-bicarbonate or sulphur solution in the early morning, reduce canopy density and avoid overhead watering.

Leaf Spot.description: Small, high-contrast dark brown lesions scattered across the blade — a classic fungal leaf-spot texture signature.
Leaf Spot.treatment: Prune infected foliage, keep leaves dry, and rotate a chlorothalonil or neem-oil treatment on a weekly cycle.

Rust Disease.description: Orange-brown pustules mixed with yellow chlorotic haloes, indicating a rust fungus colonising the underside of the leaf.
Rust Disease.treatment: Apply a triazole fungicide, clear crop debris around the plant, and avoid nitrogen over-fertilisation.

Chlorosis.description: Widespread yellowing with veins still green — nutrient chlorosis, usually iron, magnesium or nitrogen deficiency or waterlogging.
Chlorosis.treatment: Apply chelated iron or a balanced micronutrient feed, check soil pH (target 6.0–6.8) and correct drainage.

healthy.description: Chlorophyll signature is strong and evenly distributed with no significant necrotic or chlorotic pixels.
healthy.treatment: No action needed. Maintain the current irrigation and feeding schedule and re-scan in 3–5 days.

noPlant.skin: The frame looks like a person or skin tone rather than foliage — no chlorophyll signature was found.
noPlant.empty: No leaf detected. The frame has too little chlorophyll signal to analyse.
noPlant.treatment: Point the camera at a single leaf, fill most of the frame with it and keep good, even lighting.

Aphids.description: Dense clusters of small soft-bodied insects on shoots and leaf undersides, with curling leaves and sticky honeydew film.
Aphids.ipm: Release ladybird beetles or lacewings, spray neem oil (5 ml/L) or insecticidal soap early morning, and avoid excess nitrogen which drives fresh flush growth.

Stem Borer.description: Bore holes and frass at the stem node with dead-heart shoots — larvae tunnelling inside the stalk disrupt sap flow.
Stem Borer.ipm: Clip and destroy dead hearts, install pheromone traps at 5/acre, release Trichogramma egg parasitoids, and avoid ratooning infested stubble.

Whitefly.description: Tiny white winged adults lifting off the canopy when disturbed, with mottled chlorotic patches and sooty mould from honeydew.
Whitefly.ipm: Hang yellow sticky traps at 10/acre, spray neem or a horticultural oil on leaf undersides, and remove alternate weed hosts around the field bund.

Armyworm.description: Ragged window-pane feeding and skeletonised leaf blades typical of gregarious armyworm larvae feeding at night.
Armyworm.ipm: Hand-pick larvae at dusk, apply Bacillus thuringiensis or an NPV bio-pesticide, place poison-bran bait in whorls and keep field borders weed-free.

Locust.description: Heavy, coarse defoliation with whole leaf sections removed — a swarm or hopper-band grazing signature.
Locust.ipm: Alert local plant-protection authorities, use metarhizium bio-pesticide on hopper bands, run smoke/noise deterrents and shield nurseries with netting.

Bollworm.description: Circular bore holes in buds, squares or fruit with larval excreta at the entry point — classic bollworm/fruit-borer damage.
Bollworm.ipm: Install pheromone traps at 5/acre for monitoring, release Trichogramma, spray Bt or spinosad at ETL, and remove and destroy damaged squares and bolls.

clean.description: Canopy looks clean — no clustered insect bodies, bore holes or chewing damage in the colour and texture signature.
clean.ipm: No treatment needed. Keep pheromone/sticky traps in place and re-scout the block in 3–4 days.

noPlant.skin: The frame looks like a person rather than a crop — no foliage signal to inspect for pests.
noPlant.empty: No crop foliage detected in this frame, so no pest assessment could be made.
noPlant.ipm: Point the camera at the affected crop foliage, stem or fruit and fill the frame with it in even light.

water.critical: Soil is critically dry. Irrigate now with a deep watering cycle and re-check in 6 hours.
water.low: Moisture is below the healthy band. Schedule a moderate irrigation cycle within the next few hours.
water.saturated: Soil is saturated. Hold irrigation and check drainage to avoid root rot.
water.optimal: Moisture is in the optimal band. No irrigation needed — re-check in 12 hours.
